However, conventional designs either lack adequate conformability to skin or suffer from electrode fractures during skin penetration and body motion, leading to signal instability that undermines reliable multiparameter acquisition. Here, we present a fully integrated system with a soft microneedle sensor array featuring nano-hill topographies on strain-resilient electrodes to delocalize strain via geometric confinement. This design reduces signal variability by 14-fold compared to conventional designs, enabling stable, simultaneous in situ monitoring of multiple ISF biomarkers. It achieves clinical-grade accuracy for continuous glucose monitoring (mean absolute relative difference of 10.8%) and captures dynamic synchronized variations in glucose, local tissue pH, and temperature in a living subject in real time. The system integrates a reusable electronic module with a disposable microneedle array with a sensor footprint of just 1.8 cm2. By combining high signal stability with multiparameter synchrony in a compact form factor, this system offers a practical solution for reliable, real-time ISF analysis under dynamic in vivo conditions.

title: Adaptive personalization for wearable non-invasive continuous glucose sensors.
pub_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
mesh: Continuous Glucose Monitoring/instrumentation/methods; Humans; Blood Glucose/analysis; Wearable Electronic Devices; Blood Glucose Self-Monitoring/instrumentation/methods; Reproducibility of Results; Biosensing Techniques/methods/instrumentation
abstract: Accurate continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is essential for diabetes management, yet non-invasive CGM remains challenging. Universal "one-sensor-fits-all" approaches often fail, because correlations between non-invasive physiological readouts and blood glucose (BG) are highly individualized. Here, we propose a personalized "Adaptive Non-invasive CGM" methodology, which integrates a short-term minimally invasive CGM (MI-CGM) module for measuring interstitial fluid glucose, and a long-term non-invasive CGM (NI-CGM) module based on metabolic heat conformation. During a ~2-days training, the NI-CGM learns accurate sensing from the MI-CGM via GRU-based AI model, forming patient-specific sensor. The MI-CGM is then removed, leaving only the NI-CGM for long-term monitoring. In a 5-day CGM test, the system achieved MARD ~15.6%. This method also demonstrated good reproducibility and maintained reasonable accuracy (MARD ~23.9%) during long-term interval use (>2 months). This personalized approach offers a pathway from conventional "one-sensor-fits-all" strategies toward individualized sensor development, potentially mitigating inter-patient variability and non-invasive monitoring inaccuracies.

title: Container-closure Performance of an Airless Calibrated Pump for Compounded Topical Semisolids: Dispensed-mass Reproducibility, Barrier Properties, and Compatibility.
mesh: Drug Packaging/standards; Reproducibility of Results; Drug Compounding; Calibration; Metered Dose Inhalers
abstract: Primary packaging can be a critical determinant of performance for semisolid drug products, particularly when the dose is delivered by a metered device. This study evaluated an airless, pouch-based metered-dose dispenser (Topi-pump™) as a container-closure and dose-delivery system for topical semisolids, focusing on (i) packaging quality attributes, (ii) delivered-dose reproducibility, and (iii) compatibility during in-use/accelerated conditions. Packaging performance was assessed by UV-Vis light transmission (opacity), aqueous extractables screening by UV-Vis, and particulate contamination testing. Dose delivery was benchmarked against two comparable calibrated airless dispensers by quantifying the dispensed mass of semisolid vehicles under predefined handling conditions (orientation and temperature) over 10 days. The schedule comprised 40 recorded actuations per dispenser and did not extend to container exhaustion, so terminal-dose behavior was not characterized. Dispensed mass was evaluated against a 0.5 g ± 5% criterion. Compatibility was examined using model semisolids containing representative steroidal drug substances, compounded in multiple cream bases, under accelerated storage conditions, supported by microbiological testing guided by USP <61>/<62> and acceptance criteria from USP <1111>. The dispenser met predefined packaging criteria, showing low extractables (0.0050 AU; limit =0.20 AU), low particulate burden (largest particle 67 µm; criterion =100 µm), and low light transmission (opacity 0.15%; criterion =1.0%). In the pooled screening across all vehicles and operating conditions, the Topi-pump™ dispenser showed a mean dispensed mass closest to the nominal target and the lowest overall variability by coefficient of variation (screening CV 9.5% vs 18.6-21.2% for comparators), although pooled interquartile ranges were comparable for Topi-pump™ and Pump A, suggesting that the difference reflected observations outside the central portion of the distributions rather than central dispersion. Condition-level conformity and precision were subsequently evaluated within Pentravan® as a single fixed reference matrix, with apparent viscosity considered as part of the formulation context.with apparent viscosity considered as part of the formulation context. In the preliminary vehicle-level screening, using combined data from all three dispensing systems and all evaluated temperature-orientation conditions, observed conformity was 61.4% for Pentravan®, 46.
